# Repository Guidelines

## Reliability before implementation

- Before implementing, refactoring, fixing or reviewing code, read the
  [AI coding reliability guide](docs/ai-coding-reliability.md), select the rules
  triggered by the changed boundaries, and inspect the owning code and callers.
  For concurrency/lifecycle changes, trace lock order, wait dependencies, actual
  work ownership, cancellation and commit authority before editing.
- Validate the applicable failure and recovery paths, not only the happy path.
  Record concrete evidence and remaining limits; a timeout, successful build or
  passing subset is not proof that UI freezes or all deadlocks are impossible.
- When a confirmed defect exposes a reusable failure pattern, update that guide's
  existing rule or add a distinct rule with its owner and regression evidence.
  Maintain the owning contract and test selectors; keep incident logs out of the guide.

## Project Structure & Module Organization

- Four-crate Rust workspace. `crates/mesh-talk-core/` is the UI-free protocol core (lib
  `mesh_talk_core` + the `mesh-talk-node` CLI bin in `src/bin/`): feature modules `node/`,
  `identity/`, `transport/`, `discovery/`, `eventlog/`, `ratchet/`, `channel/`, `dm.rs`,
  `file/`, `postoffice/`, `storage/`. `src-tauri/` is the Tauri desktop app: entry
  `src/main.rs` → `lib.rs`, IPC glue in `commands.rs` (auth) + `chat_commands/` (messaging)
  - `events.rs`, plus `state.rs`, `tray.rs`, `services/` (auth only).
- `crates/mesh-talk-integrations/` owns scoped local messaging grants, private IPC,
  and the dedicated bot host/admin CLI; `crates/mesh-talk-mcp/` adapts its four
  send/context/status tools to the official MCP SDK. Neither owns mesh crypto.
- Integration/e2e suites live in `crates/mesh-talk-core/tests/` (`two_node_cli`,
  `persistent_history`, `post_office_offline`, `decoder_smoke`); keep unit tests inline via
  `mod tests` (e.g. `node/node_tests.rs`).
- React client sits in `frontend/src`; Vite tooling in `frontend/package.json`.
- Operational scripts in `scripts/` (`setup-hooks.sh`, `check-health.sh`); architecture in
  `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`; conventions in `specifications/`. The
  [documentation map](docs/README.md) routes readers to maintained guides; the
  [documentation guidelines](docs/DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md) define ownership
  across the README, guides, and project site.

## Build, Test, and Development Commands

- `make dev` primes Rust + Node deps and installs git hooks.
- `make build` / `make frontend-build` — release build / Vite production build.
- During feature development, preview changed-boundary validation with `make test-plan`
  and run it with `make test-changed`. Unmapped changes require an explicit owner
  and reason; inspect escalation notes for browser/native or consumer checks.
  Use `make verify-plan` / `make verify-changed` at task completion to compose the
  same affected tests with applicable formatting, lint/types and builds. The
  test-only commands do not include static checks; neither mode replaces required
  PR/review, browser/native or release gates. `make validation-report` separates
  queue and execution costs; `make validation-audit` compares a clean affected
  plan with same-source broader failure evidence before narrowing any gate.
  Read selected capability references and inspect pending browser/native requirements.
  Execution prints a structured feedback report; follow the
  [validation protocol](docs/testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities)
  for completed work, remaining evidence and additive semantic selections.
- During feature development, run affected tests only: `make test-focused
TEST_PACKAGE=mesh-talk-core TEST_FILTER=node::account_sync` selects Rust unit
  tests; add `TEST_TARGET=bridge_cross_lan` to select one integration target.
  `cd frontend && npm test -- src/features/chat/settingsDialogSession.test.ts`
  selects a frontend unit file. `make test` runs the full workspace suite
  (`cargo test --workspace`) for pre-PR and CI gates;
  `make e2e` runs the `#[ignore]`d multi-process backend rigs; `cd frontend && npm run e2e`
  runs the Playwright UI suite. Test builds use cheap KDF params (the `fast-test-kdf`
  feature), and `.cargo/config.toml` caps test/compile parallelism.
- UI / node spot checks: `make tauri-dev`, `make frontend-dev`,
  `cargo run -p mesh-talk-core --bin mesh-talk-node -- --keystore /tmp/a.keystore
--password pw --name alice` (add `--post-office` for relay mode).

## Coding Style & Naming Conventions

- Rust: `cargo fmt` (4-space, `snake_case` modules, `UpperCamelCase` types) +
  **`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`** (must match CI — `--all-targets` covers
  tests/benches).
- Frontend: `npm run format` (Prettier) + `npm run lint` (ESLint flat config).
- Write documentation and reusable prompts in English unless a specific exception is needed.
- Reference `specifications/development_conventions.md` for naming nuances.

## Domain Language

- `CONTEXT.md` is the canonical domain glossary. `docs/domain-design.md` indexes
  the modeling references and defines DDD vocabulary and naming translations.
- Distinguish local users, accounts and devices; desktop, transport and ratchet
  sessions; discovery, presence, custody, recipient delivery and read state.
- Use explicit identity/lifetime names in new code. Preserve public, wire and
  stored identifiers unless a separately validated compatibility change is intended.
- Update the glossary and affected owning guides when a domain meaning changes;
  link to definitions instead of maintaining duplicate glossaries.

## Architecture & Components

- Before adding business logic, consult [module ownership and reuse](docs/module-boundaries.md),
  inspect the owning module and its callers, and extend its existing implementation.
  Parallel tasks should name their owned paths and shared-interface dependencies;
  coordinate changes to shared interfaces through one integration owner. Keep
  feature-specific helpers local and share rules when their meaning and lifecycle
  are the same. The guide owns the detailed assignment and handoff contract.
- Stack: Rust 2024 on Tokio; Tauri 2 + React shell. No vendor-operated server.
- The `Node` (`node/node.rs`) wires identity + signed UDP **multicast** discovery
  (group `224.0.0.167`, port 47474) + Noise-encrypted TCP transport (`transport/`,
  low-level socket in `transport/net.rs`) + the content-addressed event log + DM/channel/
  file crypto. Messages are events synced as a bounded append-only log, account-addressed
  across a user's devices; optional offline custody via equal eligible post offices.
  Routed discovery and opt-in post-office federation connect reachable sites without
  joining their IP subnets. Wire formats are versioned bincode.
- See **`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`** before changing crypto, sync, or transport;
  **`docs/network-design-reference.md`** owns the communication invariants,
  module contracts, resource budgets and topology acceptance boundaries.

## Maintaining standards as requirements change

- Before changing tests, fixtures, dependencies or workflows in ways that affect
  CI cost or reliability, read [CI maintenance](docs/ci-maintenance.md). Reuse
  existing owners, measure the affected cost, and preserve acceptance evidence;
  keep required-check policy in its existing owner.
- Before implementation, identify the existing decision owner, authoritative rule,
  observable acceptance criteria, affected consumers and required boundary evidence.
  Extend the owning implementation and `validation.json`; new business capabilities
  should link their guide and invariants. Explain an unchanged contract in the PR.
- Run `make standards-check` after adding/moving source or changing contracts. It
  checks structural ownership and maintained references, including new files; it
  does not prove assertion quality, semantic completeness or candidate readiness.
  Hooks inspect the working tree, so partially staged commits still need a clean
  committed-candidate check in CI. Frontend dependencies must be installed.
- When CI exposes a local omission or flaky fixture, fix the owning selector, task
  or fixture and add a focused regression. Review timing and selection evidence
  before changing policy. Follow the maintained
  [requirement maintenance loop](docs/testing-feedback-loop.md#maintaining-standards-across-requirements).

## Testing Guidelines

- Integration coverage in `crates/mesh-talk-core/tests/` and `node/node_tests.rs`; embed
  unit tests near the code. Networking/crypto changes ship a loopback integration assertion.
- Backend multi-process E2E via `make e2e` (CI: `e2e-backend.yml`); Playwright UI E2E via
  `cd frontend && npm run e2e` (CI: `e2e-ui.yml`).
- Do not run full suites or E2E automatically during ordinary feature work. Run
  the affected unit or integration tests as changes are made; run E2E and the
  comprehensive health gate on explicit request, for optional full local preparation,
  or in CI.
- See `docs/testing-feedback-loop.md` for selection examples and escalation triggers.
- Document executed validation commands in every PR; ensure `make test` passes
  locally or through its matching CI workspace suite before merge.

## Commit & Pull Request Guidelines

- Before changing product versions or release automation, read [the version lifecycle](docs/updates.md#version-ownership-and-lifecycle).
  Root `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.package].version` is authoritative. Use
  `node scripts/release/version.mjs check|sync|prepare VERSION` (the `VERSION` argument belongs
  to `prepare` only); do not hand-edit generated npm/Cargo lock metadata or introduce another
  version constant. Root private npm metadata is a checked release-tooling projection;
  frontend private metadata is versionless and Tauri inherits Cargo. Never broadly replace
  matching dependency, fixture, history, wire or schema versions. Keep source builds `BASE-dev`,
  Nightlies `BASE-nightly.RUN.ATTEMPT`, official tagged builds `BASE`, and standard SemVer ordering.
- Version/changelog preparation and next-development-target changes use reviewed PRs. Ordinary main
  pushes must not create automatic release proposals or commit-derived product notes. Stable publication
  remains explicit through the existing verified tagged-release workflow; no direct main push,
  public empty release, mutable published tag or gate bypass. Nightly publication requires trusted
  `main` and a target above the latest Stable. Future changes must extend the existing version
  owner, its tests, standards/CI enforcement and capability contracts together; the owning guide
  documents permissions, bot-PR checks, dispatch and recovery requirements. Manual Stable draft
  preparation uses the reviewed exact-version CHANGELOG section and requires exact-source checks
  before creating its immutable tag/draft. The fixed release-history
  migration floor is historical provenance; never advance it during ordinary version bumps.

- Conventional commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`); scopes like `feat(node):` align with
  `specifications/git_standards.md`. Squash WIP; link issues. When asked to merge,
  default to squash merge unless the user explicitly requests another strategy;
  follow the [merge policy](specifications/git_standards.md#pull-request-merge-strategy)
  and current-head required checks.
- Create PRs through `./scripts/create-pr.sh -- <gh pr create options>`.
  The default checks the clean committed candidate, comparison base, argument safety,
  whitespace, cheap affected static checks, ownership blockers, structural standards,
  repository hygiene and applicable verified frontend patch coverage before publication.
  Use `make pr-check` for the same cheap static phase; missing current coverage
  evidence reports its explicit generation command and never starts suites implicitly.
  Full cross-platform CI runs after publication; all required checks must pass on the
  current PR head before merging. Creating a PR does not certify test acceptance.
- To run comprehensive checks locally before publication, use
  `./scripts/create-pr.sh --full-preflight <selectors/specs> -- <gh pr create options>`.
  This invokes `prepare-pr.sh` (platform preflight plus full health). For an existing
  PR, `./scripts/prepare-pr.sh <selectors/specs>` provides the same optional local gate.
  Use Playwright specs relevant to changed frontend behavior and repeated
  `--core-filter` / `--host-filter` / `--integration-filter` / `--mcp-filter` selectors
  for changed Rust crates. Preflight runs selected tests in Linux Docker and through
  SSH to `windows10`; Windows workspaces, caches and temporary data stay on drive D.
  Owning scenario rules add visual specs and require real native evidence for
  lifecycle/discovery changes. Missing environments or empty Rust selections fail
  full preflight. Include `e2e/ui-visual-regression.spec.ts` for theme/layout changes.
  See `docs/testing-feedback-loop.md` for configuration, coverage and plan preview.
  Fetch `origin/main` first if the comparison base is stale.
- Record focused validation and outstanding checks in the PR. Use
  `./scripts/check-health.sh` when comprehensive local evidence is needed; protected
  CI remains required before merge regardless of local results.

## Security & Adjustments

- `./scripts/check-health.sh` chains fmt, Clippy `--all-targets`, ESLint, tests, typos,
  cargo-deny, cargo-machete, gitleaks, shellcheck, audits, and both builds.
- Triage vulnerabilities immediately or document mitigation in the PR.
- If plans shift, update the relevant committed design or architecture docs. Keep
  `docs/superpowers/` and the root `plans/` directory local and untracked.

## Repository Hygiene

- Keep implementation plans, research, investigation notes and scratch scripts
  under ignored `tmp/`; remove them when the work is complete.
- Merge durable decisions into the maintained owning guide. Do not commit
  completed-work reports, score histories, duplicate runbooks or archive copies.
- `docs/evals/` owns reusable suites/inventories, prompts and its README only.
  Generated evidence belongs in ignored output or PR/CI artifacts.
- Run `node scripts/check-repository-hygiene.mjs` before committing. The shared
  index check also runs in pre-commit, CI and health, rejecting ignored files
  even when force-added. See `docs/DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md` for ownership.
# AI coding reliability guide

Use this guide before implementing or reviewing a change, especially a bug fix,
refactor, merge resolution or optimization. Its purpose is to turn recurring
failure modes into concrete design questions and executable checks. Compiling,
adding a timeout or passing a happy-path test does not establish reliability.

This guide owns the cross-cutting review method and reusable failure patterns.
[Module ownership](module-boundaries.md) owns implementation boundaries;
[architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md), [network contracts](network-design-reference.md)
and feature guides own behavior and resource limits. The
[testing workflow](testing-feedback-loop.md) owns commands, selection and gates.
Link to those owners instead of copying their changing contracts here. When code
and a contract disagree, resolve the intended behavior rather than documenting
the regression as the new rule.

## Use on every change

1. **Locate the owner and consumers.** Read the owning implementation, callers,
   existing tests and relevant guide before adding another helper or state owner.
   Include callbacks, IPC handlers, retries, startup, shutdown and recovery paths;
   an import graph alone cannot reveal all consumers.
2. **State the invariant and select risks.** Describe what must remain true on
   success, failure, cancellation and replacement. Use the table below to select
   applicable rules. A small diff can change lock order or lifetime semantics.
3. **Trace the failure path before editing.** For concurrency work, sketch who
   owns each lock, permit, task and mutable state; what it waits for; and who
   releases it. For a reproducible bug, construct a focused failing regression.
   Record unresolved hypotheses as hypotheses, not confirmed defects.
4. **Implement at the existing boundary.** Preserve authority, durable acceptance,
   compatibility and resource budgets. Recheck invariants after moving work
   outside a guard. Evaluate the proposed fix for new races and deadlocks too.
5. **Verify the changed boundary and report evidence.** Run affected checks and
   required boundary scenarios under the testing workflow. Explain results,
   exclusions and unresolved evidence. Update this guide when the defect exposes
   a reusable failure pattern; follow the maintenance procedure below.

Keep the risk explanation proportional to the change. A documentation edit does
not require a new concurrency test. A changed async callback does require a
lifetime review even when the diff is one line. Put task-specific reasoning and
results in the PR or ignored local evidence, not a new permanent report.

## Select rules by the changed boundary

| Change or symptom                                                        | Read at least                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Locks, callbacks, synchronous dispatch, UI freezes                       | [R01](#r01-lock-order-and-reentrant-calls), [R02](#r02-thread-and-scheduler-progress), [R10](#r10-evidence-that-exercises-the-failure)                |
| Background work, native providers, logout, shutdown or cancellation      | [R02](#r02-thread-and-scheduler-progress), [R03](#r03-actual-work-owns-its-lifetime), [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions)               |
| Network requests, retries, polling, queues or batches                    | [R03](#r03-actual-work-owns-its-lifetime), [R04](#r04-deadlines-cover-the-whole-operation), [R05](#r05-bounded-work-must-also-make-progress)          |
| React effects, IPC reads, dialogs, optimistic updates or mutation status | [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions), [R07](#r07-observation-is-not-mutation-ownership), [R10](#r10-evidence-that-exercises-the-failure) |
| Storage, settings, imports, deletion or recovery                         | [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions), [R08](#r08-durable-state-and-failure-semantics), [R09](#r09-bound-input-and-resource-use)          |
| IPC/API inputs, files, media or protocol changes                         | [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions), [R08](#r08-durable-state-and-failure-semantics), [R09](#r09-bound-input-and-resource-use)          |
| Merge resolution, shared helper or dependency changes                    | Revisit the affected callers and all applicable rules; a clean textual merge does not establish compatible ownership or semantics.                    |

These are starting points, not permission to ignore another reachable boundary.
Do not add a global lock, retry loop, timeout or shared abstraction solely to make
the local symptom disappear.

A frozen UI may result from a lock cycle, blocked event thread, starvation, lost
wakeup, unbounded work or stale loadin…7302 tokens truncated… macOS, four Linux/Windows); fixing the upstream failure and rerunning
the selected producers supplies that evidence, rather than omitting those OSes.

## Bound parallelism and preserve isolation

Run independent checks in parallel, but inspect each `needs` edge before removing
it: artifact availability, coverage provenance and deliberate runner admission
are real dependencies even when no explicit job output is passed. Put portable
formatting, source lint and dependency auditing on Ubuntu. Retain macOS/Windows
execution when assertions exercise their native behavior. Count macOS jobs across
all workflows against the account's actual concurrency allowance; moving one
workflow's bottleneck into another workflow's queue is not an improvement.

Use runner-owned scratch for native temporary files. Windows build/test jobs set
`TEMP` and `TMP` from `RUNNER_TEMP` in an early step, matching the local preflight
owner's explicit placement. Record old and selected paths; a different machine's
faster result does not prove that disk placement caused a prior failure. Preserve
durability, ordering and deadlines while qualifying the new hosted environment.

Full Chromium uses eight macOS partitions and four each on Linux and Windows.
Desktop browsers inherit the reusable workflow's four-slot per-OS limit; preserve
Health and WebKit admission before that burst and the existing job watchdog.
Scope limits to the actual resource pool rather than applying a macOS restriction
to Windows. Inspect late queued work after other native jobs finish; an overly
small limit can leave capacity unused. Four macOS browser jobs leave nominal room
under the five-job account limit, but do not reserve global capacity or bypass
other workflows' queues. Qualify changes on hosted runners.
Strict collectors require the platform-specific complete layout, including the
last partition, and reject layout discovery failures.

WebKit partitions retain their existing stable required-check name through a
full-union collector. Bind every producer to its actual platform, source, run and
attempt; reject missing, duplicate or stale partitions and validate the complete
scenario inventory after rebasing copied evidence. A continuously progressing
suite that exhausts its budget needs measured partitioning, not a larger timeout.

Choose shards from observed work and available runner capacity. Count setup and
artifact overhead as well as execution. More shards can increase queueing and
runner minutes; more workers per machine can increase memory pressure, port
exhaustion and test interference. Review the product of platform, architecture,
browser, feature and shard dimensions before expanding a matrix.

macOS browser coverage uses `macos-26-intel` for WebKit and Chromium, including
extended scenarios. Its contract is the macOS/browser behavior; the ARM workspace
and real native app/CLI checks retain `macos-latest`. Keep artifact labels and
per-OS collectors aligned with the actual selected image. Avoid coupling browser
admission to scarce ARM capacity needed by native builds. A job that never obtains
a runner has no test result; preserve its infrastructure failure separately.
UI coverage and reports require one complete attempt, so recover that workflow
as a whole when an unallocated producer prevents its current-attempt evidence.

ASan compiles its core library once into an official Nextest archive, then runs
eight serial partitions. The producer seals the complete default inventory and
source/compiler/config/platform identity. Trusted job outputs bind both the
manifest and archive digests; consumers reject mismatches before extraction and
compare the extracted inventory before execution. Each runner retains the same
case budgets, instrumented standard library and real clean/error controls. The
required collector checks producer success, the exhaustive disjoint inventory
and every current-attempt execution receipt. Consumer jobs do not restore the
full Rust cache or repeat the large core compilation. Keep the already compressed
archive transient and transfer it without another compression pass. Compare
producer compilation, artifact transfer, consumer preparation and queue time
alongside test execution; more shards alone can duplicate the dominant setup.
Keep extracted runtimes outside uploaded evidence. Collect receipts, inventories
and logs; do not upload another compiled binary copy from every consumer.
Attempt-bound archives and receipts require a complete sanitizer-workflow rerun
when recovering a failed attempt; do not mix a previous producer with new shards.

Retain fresh process/context isolation, owned temporary directories, dynamically
allocated ports where supported, and deterministic cleanup. Keep compile jobs,
test workers and network/rendering resource limits explicit. Do not multiply
them independently and assume the machine can absorb the combined load.
The macOS workspace coverage owner admits two compiler jobs on its small hosted
ARM runner while retaining four test workers and every target. Keep this bound
after Rust cache restoration so a scheduling experiment does not also invalidate
the cache cohort. Compare complete compile/test/resource measurements before
attributing a speedup to it; compression and swap observed across a phase do not
identify which compiler or test caused the pressure.
[Nextest archives](https://nexte.st/docs/ci-features/archiving/) can separate build
and execution, while [Playwright sharding](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-sharding)
distributes browser work. Archive consumers need the same source revision and
required runtime assets; shard distribution does not guarantee equal durations.
Both need compatible inputs and complete inventories, with isolation preserved.

Cancel superseded verification for the same candidate when safe, with concurrency
groups that separate caller workflows, event streams and branches. Reusable Health
keeps a distinct prefix because GitHub exposes the caller workflow in its context;
PR/merge candidates cancel their superseded source. Push verification uses a unique
run ID in its concurrency group: disabling cancellation alone still permits a
newer pending run to replace an older pending run. Every main commit must retain
its complete verification for release consumers, while scheduled and manual
evidence streams remain isolated. Preserve
publication and release ordering. Inspect the configured queue mode and
cancellation semantics; do not assume workflow dispatch order is execution order.
Concurrency groups do not supply merge-candidate validation. Follow GitHub's
[concurrency semantics](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency)
and the project's [merge-check rules](testing-feedback-loop.md#merge-queues-and-required-merge-checks).

## Fix instability at the owning boundary

Classify a failure before changing its budget: product regression, fixture race,
resource exhaustion, dependency/service failure or unavailable infrastructure.
Retain the failing source and attempt, first error, relevant trace and measured
phase. A passing rerun is diagnostic information, not a root-cause explanation.
Playwright explicitly [classifies a retry pass as flaky](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-retries);
keep first-attempt and retry outcomes distinct.

Synchronize with observable readiness and the exact operation being tested.
Register observers before triggering transient events; correlate signals with
request identity, immutable control state and the lifetime of the actual task.
Historical logs or a previously authenticated request do not prove that a live
request has entered the required phase. Keep cancellation, task joining and
cleanup correct on success, failure and panic.
When key ordering determines the scenario, use deterministic noncolliding fixture
identities and check actual signed keys or cursors; random IDs can exercise only
the easier path. Preserve real signing, publication and receipt assertions.
Keep commit, completed publication and recipient installation distinct. A
post-timeout snapshot can block behind the publisher and cannot prove its state
existed before the cutoff; record phases at the actual work owner.
Use the owning register-before-check notification protocol for durable status;
polling an in-memory flag can still compete with the work that must publish it.
Match a fixture's executor to its requirement: preserve single-thread tests when
responsiveness is the subject, and keep independent protocol/persistence workers
for other production-runtime scenarios. Join admitted work before deleting data.
Classify fixture gates from the current decision owner's state, not a trace flag
that also describes another phase. Do not sample a later observer projection to
decide whether to capture a one-shot event; observe that evidence before releasing
the captured task and retain its exact operation and child identity.

Separate expensive fixture preparation from the operation's measured window when
preparation is outside the requirement. Continue using the real signing,
persistence, transport or UI owner when it is part of the assertion. Preserve
production deadlines and real lifecycle coverage where those are the subject of
the test; changing the clock or injecting state cannot silently remove them.
A held real socket still consumes its production timeout while a fixture waits.
Finish unrelated cold preparation before dispatching that read, using a scoped
owned barrier before I/O where necessary. Do not pause a post-send hook to conceal
the network timeout. Consolidate repeated readiness polls into that preparation
owner; retain exact live-task and measured-operation assertions at admission.

Batch unobserved durable fixture construction through an existing validated
transaction seam when individual commit boundaries are outside the requirement.
Retain every signed event, per-event validation and index update, a completed
durable commit before observation, exact corpus assertions and the original
measured operation. Never batch away the transaction boundaries under test.
Commit CLI fixture infrastructure to its private baseline before introducing the
intended source change; unrelated copied tools must not inflate changed-file
validation or consume the assertion's watchdog.
When host tool startup is unrelated to the assertion, reuse the existing scoped
version-probe fixture rather than spawning extra version processes. Keep actual
commands and identity queries observable; do not replace the work under test.

Browser commands use the existing process owner with a deadline inside the total
job budget, reserving time for joined cleanup and evidence upload. Keep streamed
logs and append-only active/completed-case progress when final reports cannot be
written. Timeout or uncertain cleanup remains a failure. Preserve verified closure of owned work as a diagnostic separately from the
actual child outcome: Windows
intentionally terminates even an empty job to close descendant admission.
On POSIX, verify the framework's independently grouped web server as well as the
CLI group. Use its supported graceful interruption protocol; a missing teardown
acknowledgment means cleanup remains unverified. Bind lifecycle markers to the
current invocation so old evidence cannot prove a later process stopped.
Do not await output-pipe closure indefinitely after the command leader exits.
The existing process owner bounds draining after group retirement; a separately
grouped descendant retaining stdout or stderr must yield a failed structured
result with unverified cleanup and a quarantined lease. Closing owned read ends
does not prove the escaped process stopped. Keep real natural-exit, cancellation
and no-success-receipt controls rather than signalling unknown process groups.
Authorize PID cleanup only from a complete private acknowledgment, not a numeric
prefix in a stdout chunk. Stream reads do not preserve message boundaries; a
failed readiness publication must retire the child through its creation owner.
Actual CLI regression fixtures need private output directories as well as private
source directories; parallel Playwright commands otherwise delete one another's
traces and manufacture failures. Missing hosted logs do not identify a slow case.
Local-only evidence fixtures must explicitly isolate and restore inherited CI
flags, and separately assert that real CI cannot reuse local acceptance evidence.
Health captures its absolute budget before setup and uses the existing stage
owner to stop diagnostics before the job watchdog. Preserve its structured result,
execution log and bounded Node lifecycle records, including the active file/case,
through the always-upload path. Prove interruption and joined cleanup with a real
parked command. Missing hosted logs require better evidence, not a guessed fix.
Cancellation during preparation still needs a failed structured result. Only the
command owner can attest that admission never happened; failures after that
boundary must retain uncertain cleanup rather than manufacture a no-work result.

The [fixture timing guidance](testing-feedback-loop.md#cold-fixture-preparation-versus-measured-progress)
owns concrete examples and permitted boundaries.

Prefer bounded condition waits and meaningful failure diagnostics. Browser
actions should use [Playwright actionability and retrying assertions](https://playwright.dev/docs/actionability)
where applicable; application readiness may still need its own signal. Arbitrary
sleeps, broader timeouts, blanket retries and weaker assertions need evidence;
they are not default repairs for an unexplained failure. If a narrowly scoped
infrastructure retry is justified, keep its limit, original failure and outcomes
visible, and ensure repeating the operation is safe. Test retries still obey the
owning suite policy.

Keep each observation inside a polling assertion nonwaiting when the assertion
already owns readiness. A locator operation can wait for a virtualized row and
consume the entire outer budget without producing one geometry sample. Inspect
the trace to distinguish missing samples from unequal values; use one browser-side
DOM snapshot for transient geometry, treating an absent row as pending. Preserve
exact geometry and cache assertions, and exercise the absent-row control rather
than extending the deadline. The media-scroll remount regression owns this case.

For a reproducible race or timeout fix, use a regression or negative control that
fails for the original mechanism and passes with the repair. Confirm that the
intended case actually ran. Preserve existing coverage while investigating; any
temporary quarantine needs an explicit owner, reason, tracking issue and removal
condition under the existing gate policy.

## Reject incomplete discovery and generated-policy drift

Successful test execution requires successful, complete input discovery.
`scripts/ci/fuzz-targets.py` compares the discovered cargo-fuzz list with the actual
manifest-owned target inventory before running anything. Failed enumeration, an
empty list, duplicates, omissions or unknown targets fail the job, as do individual
target failures. Keep this assertion at the execution owner; shell loop command
substitution alone does not propagate discovery failure under `set -e`.

`scripts/ci/glib-migration.py` evaluates every resolved glib branch, rather than
treating a newer parallel branch as proof that an older stack was removed. Its
migration claim conservatively requires stable 0.20 or newer throughout; absent
glib and mixed old/new trees do not establish migration. The
[RustSec advisory](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2024-0429.html) owns the
security version ranges; the watcher retains native build/test and reviewed-PR
requirements before changing dependencies.

Generated native input probes share one accepted-key/extended-flag metadata owner
between WebDriver mapping and emitted C# policy. Regressions must check that every
emitted key is accepted with the correct flags and unsupported keys remain
rejected, rather than only matching the generated call text. Ownership checks and
real desktop acceptance remain separate from generator/compilation checks.

## Review the change and prevent renewed drift

Follow the existing validation stages; do not invent a parallel completion
process. For changes affecting CI behavior or recurring cost, include the
following in the normal [alignment review](maintenance-checklist.md#review-and-follow-up-procedure):

- The acceptance boundary and retained owner, including consumers affected by
  deletion, merging, selection or schedule changes.
- The measured bottleneck, comparable before/after scope and remaining unknowns;
  distinguish observed latency, resource cost and reliability.
- Executed validation and source identity, with inventory/provenance checks or
  regression controls appropriate to the changed mechanism.
- Remaining hosted, cross-platform, native or release evidence and the owner of
  any follow-up. Do not claim candidate acceptance from local or older results.

Workflow, runner and tool upgrades can change CLI semantics, report formats,
selectors and archive compatibility. Validate affected real tool invocations and
failure paths through the existing diagnostic owners; YAML parsing or unit mocks
alone do not establish the behavior of the installed tool.

Consolidate frontend unit execution through the complete Linux coverage owner
when the ordinary and coverage commands select the same inventory and platform
branches use explicit mocks. Verify that inventory with the actual runner before
removing duplicate OS executions. Retain real browser/native matrices and native
diagnostic fixtures; mocked platform branches do not supply those contracts.
Keep Node/filesystem portability requirements in their owning diagnostics rather
than duplicating the entire frontend unit suite incidentally.

Keep platform-exclusive probes in the required native producer that can execute
them. Universal local selections must not include a file whose entire suite is
skipped on other hosts; preserve the nonempty-test guard and explicit native
escalation instead. Keep workflow wiring assertions in the cheap CI policy
owner, separate from the underlying tool's filesystem/compiler regressions.

After pushing, observe the actual hosted candidate until the relevant jobs finish.
Compare before and after setup time, test time, required-check latency and runner
minutes with sample sizes and cache conditions. Inspect first failures and queue
changes, then make another measured pass when evidence identifies remaining waste.
A pushed branch, a local green subset, or a faster isolated step does not establish
an end-to-end speedup. Keep the candidate reviewable and continue in a clean
worktree when unrelated local edits prevent publication; do not discard those
edits or treat them as a reason to stop the optimization.

Revisit timing and failure evidence when a gate becomes slower, starts rerunning,
gains another platform/dependency, or repeatedly exceeds its expected budget.
During existing maintenance reviews, inspect slow cases, duplicated setup,
shard imbalance, cache churn and abandoned temporary exceptions. Retire obsolete
work with its consumers and selectors rather than accumulating permanent layers.

Keep this review proportional: a documentation-only change needs applicable
formatting, links and structural checks, not a new build benchmark. Rules should
be enforceable through existing contracts and diagnostics where practical;
adding this guide does not create a scheduled job or another required check.
"}

---
name: test-driven-development
description: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code
---

# Test-Driven Development (TDD)

## Overview

Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.

**Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.

**Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**

## When to Use

**Always:**
- New features
- Bug fixes
- Refactoring
- Behavior changes

**Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
- Throwaway prototypes
- Generated code
- Configuration files

Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.

## The Iron Law

```
NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
```

Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.

**No exceptions:**
- Don't keep it as "reference"
- Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
- Don't look at it
- Delete means delete

Implement fresh from tests. Period.

## Red-Green-Refactor

```dot
digraph tdd_cycle {
    rankdir=LR;
    red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
    verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
    green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
    verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
    refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
    next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];

    red -> verify_red;
    verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
    verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
    green -> verify_green;
    verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
    verify_green -> green [label="no"];
    refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
    verify_green -> next;
    next -> red;
}
```

### RED - Write Failing Test

Write one minimal test showing what should happen.

<Good>
```typescript
test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
  let attempts = 0;
  const operation = () => {
    attempts++;
    if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
    return 'success';
  };

  const result = await retryOperation(operation);

  expect(result).toBe('success');
  expect(attempts).toBe(3);
});
```
Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
test('retry works', async () => {
  const mock = jest.fn()
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
  await retryOperation(mock);
  expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
});
```
Vague name, tests mock not code
</Bad>

**Requirements:**
- One behavior
- Clear name
- Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)

### Verify RED - Watch It Fail

**MANDATORY. Never skip.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test fails (not errors)
- Failure message is expected
- Fails because feature missing (not typos)

**Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.

**Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.

### GREEN - Minimal Code

Write simplest code to pass the test.

<Good>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      if (i === 2) throw e;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('unreachable');
}
```
Just enough to pass
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
  options?: {
    maxRetries?: number;
    backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential';
    onRetry?: (attempt: number) => void;
  }
): Promise<T> {
  // YAGNI
}
```
Over-engineered
</Bad>

Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.

### Verify GREEN - Watch It Pass

**MANDATORY.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test passes
- Other tests still pass
- Output pristine (no errors, warnings)

**Test fails?** Fix code, not test.

**Other tests fail?** Fix now.

### REFACTOR - Clean Up

After green only:
- Remove duplication
- Improve names
- Extract helpers

Keep tests green. Don't add behavior.

### Repeat

Next failing test for next feature.

## Good Tests

| Quality | Good | Bad |
|---------|------|-----|
| **Minimal** | One thing. "and" in name? Split it. | `test('validates email and domain and whitespace')` |
| **Clear** | Name describes behavior | `test('test1')` |
| **Shows intent** | Demonstrates desired API | Obscures what code should do |

## Why Order Matters

**"I'll write tests after to verify it works"**

Tests written after code pass immediately. Passing immediately proves nothing:
- Might test wrong thing
- Might test implementation, not behavior
- Might miss edge cases you forgot
- You never saw it catch the bug

Test-first forces you to see the test fail, proving it actually tests something.

**"I already manually tested all the edge cases"**

Manual testing is ad-hoc. You think you tested everything but:
- No record of what you tested
- Can't re-run when code changes
- Easy to forget cases under pressure
- "It worked when I tried it" ≠ comprehensive

Automated tests are systematic. They run the same way every time.

**"Deleting X hours of work is wasteful"**

Sunk cost fallacy. The time is already gone. Your choice now:
- Delete and rewrite with TDD (X more hours, high confidence)
- Keep it and add tests after (30 min, low confidence, likely bugs)

The "waste" is keeping code you can't trust. Working code without real tests is technical debt.

**"TDD is dogmatic, being pragmatic means adapting"**

TDD IS pragmatic:
- Finds bugs before commit (faster than debugging after)
- Prevents regressions (tests catch breaks immediately)
- Documents behavior (tests show how to use code)
- Enables refactoring (change freely, tests catch breaks)

"Pragmatic" shortcuts = debugging in production = slower.

**"Tests after achieve the same goals - it's spirit not ritual"**

No. Tests-after answer "What does this do?" Tests-first answer "What should this do?"

Tests-after are biased by your implementation. You test what you built, not what's required. You verify remembered edge cases, not discovered ones.

Tests-first force edge case discovery before implementing. Tests-after verify you remembered everything (you didn't).

30 minutes of tests after ≠ TDD. You get coverage, lose proof tests work.

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Too simple to test" | Simple code breaks. Test takes 30 seconds. |
| "I'll test after" | Tests passing immediately prove nothing. |
| "Tests after achieve same goals" | Tests-after = "what does this do?" Tests-first = "what should this do?" |
| "Already manually tested" | Ad-hoc ≠ systematic. No record, can't re-run. |
| "Deleting X hours is wasteful" | Sunk cost fallacy. Keeping unverified code is technical debt. |
| "Keep as reference, write tests first" | You'll adapt it. That's testing after. Delete means delete. |
| "Need to explore first" | Fine. Throw away exploration, start with TDD. |
| "Test hard = design unclear" | Listen to test. Hard to test = hard to use. |
| "TDD will slow me down" | TDD faster than debugging. Pragmatic = test-first. |
| "Manual test faster" | Manual doesn't prove edge cases. You'll re-test every change. |
| "Existing code has no tests" | You're improving it. Add tests for existing code. |

## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over

- Code before test
- Test after implementation
- Test passes immediately
- Can't explain why test failed
- Tests added "later"
- Rationalizing "just this once"
- "I already manually tested it"
- "Tests after achieve the same purpose"
- "It's about spirit not ritual"
- "Keep as reference" or "adapt existing code"
- "Already spent X hours, deleting is wasteful"
- "TDD is dogmatic, I'm being pragmatic"
- "This is different because..."

**All of these mean: Delete code. Start over with TDD.**

## Example: Bug Fix

**Bug:** Empty email accepted

**RED**

description: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code

# Test-Driven Development (TDD)

## Overview

Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.

**Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.

**Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**

## When to Use

**Always:**
- New features
- Bug fixes
- Refactoring
- Behavior changes

**Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
- Throwaway prototypes
- Generated code
- Configuration files

Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.

## The Iron Law

```
NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
```

Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.

**No exceptions:**
- Don't keep it as "reference"
- Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
- Don't look at it
- Delete means delete

Implement fresh from tests. Period.

## Red-Green-Refactor

```dot
digraph tdd_cycle {
    rankdir=LR;
    red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
    verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
    green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
    verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
    refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
    next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];

    red -> verify_red;
    verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
    verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
    green -> verify_green;
    verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
    verify_green -> green [label="no"];
    refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
    verify_green -> next;
    next -> red;
}
```

### RED - Write Failing Test

Write one minimal test showing what should happen.

<Good>
```typescript
test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
  let attempts = 0;
  const operation = () => {
    attempts++;
    if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
    return 'success';
  };

  const result = await retryOperation(operation);

  expect(result).toBe('success');
  expect(attempts).toBe(3);
});
```
Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
test('retry works', async () => {
  const mock = jest.fn()
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
  await retryOperation(mock);
  expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
});
```
Vague name, tests mock not code
</Bad>

**Requirements:**
- One behavior
- Clear name
- Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)

### Verify RED - Watch It Fail

**MANDATORY. Never skip.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test fails (not errors)
- Failure message is expected
- Fails because feature missing (not typos)

**Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.

**Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.

### GREEN - Minimal Code

Write simplest code to pass the test.

<Good>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      if (i === 2) throw e;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('unreachable');
}
```
Just enough to pass
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
  options?: {
    maxRetries?: number;
    backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential';
    onRetry?: (attempt: number) => void;
  }
): Promise<T> {
  // YAGNI
}
```
Over-engineered
</Bad>

Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.

### Verify GREEN - Watch It Pass

**MANDATORY.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test passes
- Other tests still pass
- Output pristine (no errors, warnings)

**Test fails?** Fix code, not test.

**Other tests fail?** Fix now.

### REFACTOR - Clean Up

After green only:
- Remove duplication
- Improve names
- Extract helpers

Keep tests green. Don't add behavior.

### Repeat

Next failing test for next feature.

## Good Tests

| Quality | Good | Bad |
|---------|------|-----|
| **Minimal** | One thing. "and" in name? Split it. | `test('validates email and domain and whitespace')` |
| **Clear** | Name describes behavior | `test('test1')` |
| **Shows intent** | Demonstrates desired API | Obscures what code should do |

## Why Order Matters

**"I'll write tests after to verify it works"**

Tests written after code pass immediately. Passing immediately proves nothing:
- Might test wrong thing
- Might test implementation, not behavior
- Might miss edge cases you forgot
- You never saw it catch the bug

Test-first forces you to see the test fail, proving it actually tests something.

**"I already manually tested all the edge cases"**

Manual testing is ad-hoc. You think you tested everything but:
- No record of what you tested
- Can't re-run when code changes
- Easy to forget cases under pressure
- "It worked when I tried it" ≠ comprehensive

Automated tests are systematic. They run the same way every time.

**"Deleting X hours of work is wasteful"**

Sunk cost fallacy. The time is already gone. Your choice now:
- Delete and rewrite with TDD (X more hours, high confidence)
- Keep it and add tests after (30 min, low confidence, likely bugs)

The "waste" is keeping code you can't trust. Working code without real tests is technical debt.

**"TDD is dogmatic, being pragmatic means adapting"**

TDD IS pragmatic:
- Finds bugs before commit (faster than debugging after)
- Prevents regressions (tests catch breaks immediately)
- Documents behavior (tests show how to use code)
- Enables refactoring (change freely, tests catch breaks)

"Pragmatic" shortcuts = debugging in production = slower.

**"Tests after achieve the same goals - it's spirit not ritual"**

No. Tests-after answer "What does this do?" Tests-first answer "What should this do?"

Tests-after are biased by your implementation. You test what you built, not what's required. You verify remembered edge cases, not discovered ones.

Tests-first force edge case discovery before implementing. Tests-after verify you remembered everything (you didn't).

30 minutes of tests after ≠ TDD. You get coverage, lose proof tests work.

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Too simple to test" | Simple code breaks. Test takes 30 seconds. |
| "I'll test after" | Tests passing immediately prove nothing. |
| "Tests after achieve same goals" | Tests-after = "what does this do?" Tests-first = "what should this do?" |
| "Already manually tested" | Ad-hoc ≠ systematic. No record, can't re-run. |
| "Deleting X hours is wasteful" | Sunk cost fallacy. Keeping unverified code is technical debt. |
| "Keep as reference, write tests first" | You'll adapt it. That's testing after. Delete means delete. |
| "Need to explore first" | Fine. Throw away exploration, start with TDD. |
| "Test hard = design unclear" | Listen to test. Hard to test = hard to use. |
| "TDD will slow me down" | TDD faster than debugging. Pragmatic = test-first. |
| "Manual test faster" | Manual doesn't prove edge cases. You'll re-test every change. |
| "Existing code has no tests" | You're improving it. Add tests for existing code. |

## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over

- Code before test
- Test after implementation
- Test passes immediately
- Can't explain why test failed
- Tests added "later"
- Rationalizing "just this once"
- "I already manually tested it"
- "Tests after achieve the same purpose"
- "It's about spirit not ritual"
- "Keep as reference" or "adapt existing code"
- "Already spent X hours, deleting is wasteful"
- "TDD is dogmatic, I'm being pragmatic"
- "This is different because..."

**All of these mean: Delete code. Start over with TDD.**

## Example: Bug Fix

**Bug:** Empty email accepted

**RED**
```typescript
test('rejects empty email', async () => {
  const result = await submitForm({ email: '' });
  expect(result.error).toBe('Email required');
});
```

**Verify RED**
```bash
$ npm test
FAIL: expected 'Email required', got undefined
```

**GREEN**
```typescript
function submitForm(data: FormData) {
  if (!data.email?.trim()) {
    return { error: 'Email required' };
  }
  // ...
}
```

**Verify GREEN**
```bash
$ npm test
PASS
```

**REFACTOR**
Extract validation for multiple fields if needed.

## Verification Checklist

Before marking work complete:

- [ ] Every new function/method has a test
- [ ] Watched each test fail before implementing
- [ ] Each test failed for expected reason (feature missing, not typo)
- [ ] Wrote minimal code to pass each test
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
- [ ] Tests use real code (mocks only if unavoidable)
- [ ] Edge cases and errors covered

Can't check all boxes? You skipped TDD. Start over.

## When Stuck

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Don't know how to test | Write wished-for API. Write assertion first. Ask your human partner. |
| Test too complicated | Design too complicated. Simplify interface. |
| Must mock everything | Code too coupled. Use dependency injection. |
| Test setup huge | Extract helpers. Still complex? Simplify design. |

## Debugging Integration

Bug found? Write failing test reproducing it. Follow TDD cycle. Test proves fix and prevents regression.

Never fix bugs without a test.

## Testing Anti-Patterns

When adding mocks or test utilities, read @testing-anti-patterns.md to avoid common pitfalls:
- Testing mock behavior instead of real behavior
- Adding test-only methods to production classes
- Mocking without understanding dependencies

## Final Rule

```
Production code → test exists and failed first
Otherwise → not TDD
```

No exceptions without your human partner's permission.

## R04: Deadlines cover the whole operation

**Failure pattern:** each route or phase has a timeout, but queueing, admission,
serial alternatives or retries make the complete user operation effectively
unbounded. A generic timeout error also triggers the wrong retry/recovery path.

Use the existing owning budget for the whole logical operation, including permit
waits and all alternatives; carry its remaining time into subordinate work where
needed. Distinguish observation deadlines, admission refusal and transport failure.
Preserve the owner-defined retry policy and original operation identity. Do not
reset the overall budget on every attempt or increase it just to hide a hang.

Check cancellation cleanup and late completion as well as elapsed time. Async
timers cannot interrupt a thread blocked in a synchronous mutex, native call or
filesystem syscall. Such a path also needs R01–R03. Budget values remain in the
[network contracts](network-design-reference.md#8-resource-budgets-compatibility-and-performance)
and implementation, rather than a second set of constants here.

**Evidence:** stall admission and a later network phase separately, use multiple
candidate routes, and verify permits/socket owners are released. Check that an
expired preflight has no partial durable mutation. Examples live in
[privacy runtime tests](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/privacy_runtime_tests.rs)
and [group invitation tests](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_group/tests.rs).

## R05: Bounded work must also make progress
## R10: Evidence that exercises the failure

Source-order contracts must assert that each required command exists before
comparing its position. A missing substring returns a sentinel such as `-1` and
can otherwise make an ordering assertion pass vacuously. Match the canonical
command owner and keep actual execution controls for behavior beyond routing.

Browser fixtures must make hydrated backend settings agree with the intended
frontend state before navigation; a later settings response must not silently
remove the capability under test. The call-readiness fixture owns that setup.
For saved reading positions, exhausting bounded animation-frame polling does not
prove geometry is ready: retain the conversation-owned target and resume on
geometry changes, cancelling observers on cleanup and reader intent. The viewport
unit regression supplies geometry only after the polling window.

Raw storage injection in concurrency fixtures must publish through the normal
owner notification before requiring a peer's unrelated scope to settle. Preserve
the protected in-flight page, exact inventory assertions and original latency
bounds; the same-source control fixture owns this preparation contract. Finish
unrelated readiness preparation before dispatching a timed network read. A
protected task can still reach its genuine idle deadline. Test barriers belong
before I/O, inside the owned child, with cancellation releasing their futures;
post-send hooks must not hide that deadline. Do not repeat long preparation waits
inside the measured held-read window.

Concurrent actual-tool fixtures must own output directories, not only source
and temporary data. A second Playwright invocation can otherwise clean a running
suite's traces. The browser command owner retains live logs and case progress,
joins descendants before reporting and fails on timeout or uncertain retirement.

Keep a test's observation scope equal to its named requirement. The
growing-history fixture measures exact durable originals during continuation,
then checks the full public
projection after retiring its continuously appending peers. Its projection read
must not compete with an endless writer inside the continuation latency bound.
Paused-clock maintenance tests wait for actual retry attempts and assert minimum
backoff spacing; real measured database duty time cannot imply a fixed number of
attempts inside an arbitrary virtual-time window. Preserve cancellation, other
maintenance-class progress and the no-early-retry assertions.

Prefer one qualified scenario for a requirement over repeated whole-host
variants with weaker preparation. The same-source control receipt owner retains
its five prepared partial-corpus Noise scenarios, including the exact live child
at admission, both preserved checkpoints, unchanged eight-second receipt,
cancellation and post-release recovery. Its former empty-corpus duplicate could
lose a natural read between setup notification and admission; removing that
variant does not qualify a separate fresh empty-corpus timing boundary. Keep the
retired-child observer and interrupted-preparation controls rather than adding
sleep, suppressing publication or accepting a stale child to rescue setup.
Its test-only dispatch gate must classify the actual owed parked pair credit,
not the shared resumed trace label. Capture that one-shot child before waiting
for its later projection; retain exact private-receipt evidence before release.
The paid-pair classifier regression rejects foreground resumes and unprotected
turns while the real Noise scenarios retain admission and recovery assertions.
When inventory ordering selects a different continuation path, construct canonical
signed fixture events with noncolliding deterministic identifiers and assert the
actual persisted key ordering. Distinguish durable commit, completed publication
and recipient installation in timing evidence; a publication-begin trace is not
proof of completion. Preserve bounded owner-phase diagnostics through recovery
without extending the measured deadline or warming away the required cold work.

A progressing serial test partition can exhaust its job watchdog without a hung
case. The Windows archive owner uses eight native serial execution partitions,
with direct required checks and the existing sealed once-only inventory contract.
Exercise actual pinned archive consumers and omission/duplication/failed-execution
controls. Preserve watchdogs, product assertions and full coverage. The existing
protection migration owner requires every successful current-head app-bound
replacement before retiring oversized partition names; skipped or partial runs
cannot qualify. Account for additional archive/setup cost and hosted variation.
The shared union verifier takes the caller-owned partition count; Windows capacity
changes must not alter the independent eight-part ASan contract. Run both real-tool
protocol fixtures and their missing/duplicate/failed-receipt controls. ASan
compilation reuse must bind the source, platform, compiler and archive/manifest
digests through trusted producer outputs. Reject changed bytes and inventories
before running archived tests; fresh-consumer controls must prove execution
without producer build outputs. Retain real instrumentation checks on each runner.

A total functional browser-case watchdog is not a product performance SLA.
Trace the failed interval: when several individually successful cold-load,
rendering and interaction steps exhaust the total, use the existing generous
functional allowance consistently across platforms. Preserve individual
assertion bounds and explicit latency contracts. The real Playwright watchdog
control derives the actual source configuration, accelerates only its duration,
and requires timeout failure plus later-case execution with joined descendants;
never disable the watchdog or use retries to qualify a failure.

Independent message kinds should have independent browser scenarios. The
[automatic delivery fixture](../frontend/e2e/automatic-delivery.spec.ts) checks
text, sticker and file-card Awaiting/explicit projection separately; keep the
file disclosure and keyboard assertions in its file case. Three unrelated send
journeys can exhaust one functional watchdog before their final assertion.
Update the authoritative browser inventory alongside the split, retaining strict
trace/error evidence and every kind's confirmation predicate.

Functional browser scenarios should use the smallest data set that exercises
all named state transitions. Recovery-batch navigation needs distinct partial
and terminal deliveries plus concurrent live and duplicate signals; repeated
extra rows only multiply traced render work. Keep the separate large-history
window case and deterministic announcement-coalescing/deduplication tests in
[conversation reception](group-conversation-reception.md).

Use barriers, deferred promises, injected provider/storage stalls and controlled
clocks at the actual boundary. Prefer an observable progress assertion to an
arbitrary sleep or a test that checks only that a timeout helper was called.
Verify successful behavior, failure, cleanup and replacement through the same
production owner; a mock that bypasses the problematic lock proves little.

The group-inventory held-peer fixture rejects a real authenticated setup
exchange before admitting its independent publication measurement. Snapshot
exact-peer/group begin and end counters only after the actual Fingerprint hold
enters; require exactly one live round, unchanged counters and an open transport
through the original eight-second publication bound. A setup failure is not a
measured-window completion. A server task parked after client EOF is not a live
hold; observe transport retirement and join it on cancellation. The owner is
`group_inventory_publication_progresses_while_unrelated_peer_sync_is_held` in
`account_documents/tests.rs`, selected by core-account-group validation.

Give connection setup and capability negotiation their own bounded watchdog.
Start a progress deadline only after the required stalled operation is admitted,
and prove the competing work is still incomplete at that point. Release only
that work's barrier while retaining the stall. Measure cancellation separately
from setup and history progress; preserve each behavior's required bound.

A periodic probe can miss readiness between its last check and the deadline.
Use [R05](#r05-bounded-work-must-also-make-progress)'s waiter protocol to recheck
the actual condition on a transition, retaining the original deadline and bounded
fallback. A snapshot taken after timeout is diagnostic evidence, not success.

An offline fixture that needs prompt connection failure must own and observe
actual transport closure; reserving a TCP port does not guarantee refusal or
retire a pending dial. The [own-copy fixture](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/delivery_runtime_tests.rs)
qualifies real accept-and-close behavior, joins its unavailable-endpoint owner,
then hands the same listener to the cold application without changing its
confirmation budget.

A direct protocol fixture must own its cold-start preconditions. Starting every
background repair loop can negotiate or import the claimed first request before
the explicit operation and consume its transport capacity. Reuse the bounded
[inbound connection owner](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/serving.rs) when the
scenario drives requests directly; keep full-host recovery tests separate. The
[certificate refresh fixture](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_documents/tests.rs)
requires no prior sibling negotiation or imported custody key, then positively
witnesses its real explicit negotiation and durable projection. It commits its
baseline without fanout and explicitly drives each real sync/Have exchange before
observing custody. A passive observer cannot advance pending work when the
fixture deliberately has no autonomous recovery owner.

Keep fixture validation at the narrow boundary it owns. A full-host scenario
whose only assertion concerns another test helper adds unrelated synchronization
and scheduling prerequisites without a product oracle. Reuse the real protocol
and business scenarios instead: [Wake authentication and recovery controls](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_sync/selection_tests.rs)
own linked identity, revision deduplication and notification-driven convergence;
[custody scenarios](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_documents/tests.rs)
own authenticated preparation, held-domain independence and durable custody.
Custody accounting preparation uses serial real channel-document requests on
inbound-only peers before autonomous workers start. A mutable whole-Optional or
Wake-settled snapshot is not a prerequisite for that accounting contract: it can
restart and create unrelated capacity contention while an observer waits. Remove
the global observer and its helper-only full-host tests; retain signed channel
floors, exact-peer capabilities and the real automatic custody/offline controls.
Do not add a clock switch solely to rescue a helper's self-test. Keep a loopback
business scenario focused on its named behavior. The member-invitation proof
ends after epoch delivery, pre-join isolation and role rejection. Existing
focused transfer/authority controls own ownership changes; the small two-node
departure proof owns actual offline pause/relaunch and retry of the original
signed event and parent cut. Do not chain unrelated controls and reconnection
requirements onto an already complete invitation scenario.

A fixture with a live authoritative identity observer must not simulate account
replacement by changing only a derived UI store. A later valid backend observation
can restore that store. Keep the [startup browser proof](../frontend/e2e/theme-picker.spec.ts)
focused on startup and real logout/relogin; the [scoped pack](../frontend/src/store/packs.test.ts)
and [linked appearance](../frontend/src/lib/linkedAppearance.test.ts) controls own
replacement and stale callbacks. A browser test of an actual account transition
must change its authoritative identity boundary consistently.

Keep a scheduling control's corpus at the protocol boundary it needs. The
[queued-source controls](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_group/tests/selected_queued_source_control_latency.rs)
use a normal short partial page and retain strict result/checkpoint ordering;
separate real-protocol tests own full-page durability and replay. Qualify request
liveness before its cancellation trigger and the actual resumed owner before
admission. A cancellation-triggering publication need not leave the old request
alive after the publisher returns.

Browser device options express intent; they do not observe native input state.
Establish the required device mode through the browser's supported emulation
owner, then verify actual media queries and touch capabilities before measuring
responsive hit areas. Do not replace `matchMedia` with a JavaScript mock. The
[touch fixture](../frontend/e2e/touch-targets.spec.ts) exercises controlled native
state loss, actual CSS target sizes and a real tap through that same owner.
A negative control must observe the capability it removes; disabling touch does
not require every host to become hover-capable or shrink its CSS targets.

A deadlock regression must not hang its own runner: bound coordination, arrange
fixture release even when assertions fail, and use an isolated process with an
outer deadline when a synchronous lock cycle cannot be safely unwound. An async
timeout inside the blocked thread is not sufficient. Avoid port-selection races
and process-global fixtures that assume serial execution; respect the repository's
test environment and resource controls.

Intentional cancellation and output-limit controls need an independent process
owner. Inheriting the real runner's owner marker can terminate the enclosing
validation instead of only the synthetic command. The
[process-owner fixture](../scripts/diagnostics/windows-process-owner.test.mjs)
checks both the retained output-limit failure and successful enclosing supervisor
through an actual nested execution.

Treat a lock-order suspicion, a reproduced bug and a passing regression as
different evidence. A stack sample or total suite duration alone does not prove
one test is deadlocked. Inspect the active operation, its duration and the actual
wait dependencies. Preserve required assertions when fixing flaky setup; do not
hide a failure with retries, larger sleeps, skipped tests or weaker selectors.

Record the tested source, command, environment, count and outcome. Reassess
consumers after merging new callers or changing a shared helper. Static scans,
passing unit tests and browser IPC mocks do not establish native OS behavior or

remain distinct from passes. Completed individual commands do not turn a cancelled
parent run into a passing full gate. Verification collectors must release cancelled workflows while still rejecting

and block its replacement in the concurrency group. The
[CI maintenance guide](ci-maintenance.md) owns this scheduling rule;
[merge-queue regressions](../scripts/diagnostics/merge-queue.test.mjs) exercise
eligibility after failure and ineligibility after cancellation. Follow the
[validation protocol](testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities)
and keep unresolved native, cross-platform and stress obligations explicit.
